candidates.title: Rethinking I/O Caching for Large Language Model Inference on Resource-Constrained Mobile Platforms
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have traditionally relegated inference to remote servers, leaving mobile devices as thin clients. Recently, advances in mobile GPUs and NPUs have made on-device inference increasingly feasible, particularly for privacy-sensitive and personalized applications. However, executing LLMs directly on resource-constrained devices exposes severe I/O bottlenecks, as repeated accesses to large weight files can overwhelm limited memory and storage bandwidth. Prior studies have focused on internal mechanisms such as KV caching, while the role of the host OS buffer cache remains underexplored. This paper closes that gap with file-level trace analysis of real-world mobile LLM applications, and identifies three characteristic access patterns: (1) one-time sequential scans during initialization, (2) persistent hot sets (e.g., tokenizers, metadata, indices), and (3) recurring loop accesses to model weight files. Guided by these observations, we propose LLM-aware buffer cache strategies and derive cache-sizing guidelines that relate loop size, host-set coverage, and storage bandwidth. We further compare smartwatch-class and smartphone-class platforms to clarify feasible model sizes and practical hardware prerequisites for local inference. Our results provide system-level guidance for I/O subsystem design that enables practical on-device LLM inference in future mobile and IoT devices.
candidates.reason: モバイル端末上のLLM推論で重みファイルへの反復アクセスが起こすI/Oボトルネックを実アプリのファイルレベルトレースで分析し、初期化時の一括走査・常駐ホットセット・重みループアクセスという3パターンを特定して、LLM向けOSバッファキャッシュ戦略とサイズ指針を導いたオンデバイス推論のI/O研究である。

candidates.title: MaaI: ML-as-an-Infrastructure for Diverse Personalized Inference With Edge Offloading
candidates.abstract: The rapid advancements in large language models (LLMs) have transformed applications across industries, from natural language understanding to content generation. However, their escalating computational demands and dependence on cloud services create barriers to the widespread adoption of customized models. We introduce MaaI, an edge-offloading architecture that optimizes LLM deployment by distributing computational tasks and customization across edge devices and cloud servers. Crucially, MaaI identifies the optimal partition point to divide the model between the server and edge, ensuring that foundational components are allocated to edge devices while intensive computations remain in the cloud. Utilizing quantization and LoRA adapters, this approach enables users to leverage larger models with enhanced performance while minimizing server load. Furthermore, by retaining only the foundational model on the server and offloading customized adaptations to edge devices, MaaI facilitates scalable, personalized deployments without significantly increasing server resource requirements. Experimental results across diverse benchmarks and hardware configurations confirm MaaI’s effectiveness in optimizing performance, memory efficiency, and latency.
candidates.reason: カスタマイズ済みLLMの展開をクラウド依存から解くため、基盤部分をエッジ・重い計算をクラウドに分ける最適分割点を求め、量子化とLoRAアダプタを組み合わせたエッジオフロード基盤MaaIを提案し、性能・メモリ効率・レイテンシの改善を実証した推論基盤研究である。

candidates.title: Effective Rank-Based Layer-Wise Low-Rank Approximation for LLMs
candidates.venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
candidates.abstract: Post-training compression of large language models (LLMs) is moving from heuristic ratios toward interpretable, layer-wise policies. We propose a unified, training-free low-rank pipeline that (i) uses an information-theoretic effective rank to set the retained rank k per layer, (ii) constructs layer-wise second-order statistics from a WikiText-2 calibration set (256×4096) and applies right-multiplicative whitening to obtain a better-conditioned factorization domain, (iii) performs SVD on the whitened weight WL and maps the approximation back to the original domain via right-multiplying L−1, and (iv) realizes deployment as two linear factors by splitting the truncated diagonal term. On LLaMA-2-7B, we systematically evaluate decompositions of Gate, Up, Down, and their combinations by using perplexity (PPL), and activation-distribution statistics. Under the same effective-rank policy, whitened-domain decomposition is more robust (e.g., PPL 7.45→≈8.02) than direct decomposition in the original domain (PPL up to 8.38); effective rank serves as a practical lower bound for singular-value retention, offering a consistent, transferable truncation starting point across layers; and clear layer heterogeneity emerges that Gate/Up are more amenable to low-rank approximation, whereas Down is more sensitive and benefits from larger k or conservative handling. Rather than pursuing extreme compression, this work validates the compressibility boundary of LLM weights and provides an interpretable truncation policy, forming a clean interface and engineering baseline for composite compression with quantization, pruning, and distillation.
candidates.reason: 情報理論的な実効ランクで層ごとの保持ランクを決め、キャリブレーション統計によるホワイトニング領域でSVDを行う学習不要の層別低ランク近似パイプラインを提案し、2つの線形因子としてそのままデプロイできる形でLLM重み圧縮の解釈可能な截断方針を示した、推論向け圧縮の研究である。
